label: Docker MCP Server
replaces: Replaces repeated shell invocations of `docker` and `docker-compose` (container inspection, logs, compose lifecycle) with structured MCP tool calls.
rationale: Container logs, inspect JSON, and ps tables executed via shell flood the context window with verbose formatting; Docker MCP tools return scoped container status and structured metadata, reducing re-runs and parsing errors.

label: Git MCP Server
replaces: Replaces repeated shell invocations of `git` (status, diff, log, branch, commit) with structured MCP tool calls.
rationale: Repeated git status, log, and diff shell calls often require extra flags and formatting retries; Git MCP exposes typed repository operations with explicit repo paths and bounded diff context.

label: GitHub MCP Server
replaces: Replaces repeated shell invocations of the `gh` CLI (issues, pull requests, workflow runs, releases) with structured MCP tool calls.
rationale: The gh CLI mixes human-formatted tables with ad-hoc --json and --jq queries that frequently fail or truncate fields; the official GitHub MCP server provides typed issue, PR, and repository endpoints directly.

label: Kubernetes MCP Server
replaces: Replaces repeated shell invocations of `kubectl` (pod status, logs, events, resource inspection) with structured MCP tool calls.
rationale: Cluster debugging through kubectl requires chaining namespace flags, jsonpath expressions, and log tails; a Kubernetes MCP server exposes contexts, events, and pod logs with built-in read-only and context-allowlist guards.

label: PostgreSQL MCP Server
replaces: Replaces repeated shell invocations of `psql` for schema inspection, explain plans, and SQL queries with structured MCP tool calls.
rationale: Running psql through the shell requires escaping SQL strings and parsing ASCII tables; a dedicated PostgreSQL MCP server provides schema introspection, query plans, and restricted read-only access modes.

label: MySQL MCP Server
replaces: Replaces repeated shell invocations of `mysql` for schema discovery and SQL queries with structured MCP tool calls.
rationale: Shell mysql commands depend on brittle quoting and tabular text output; a dedicated MySQL MCP server returns structured query rows and enforces explicit per-schema read/write permissions.

label: SQLite MCP Server
replaces: Replaces repeated shell invocations of `sqlite3` for local database inspection and SQL queries with structured MCP tool calls.
rationale: Repeated sqlite3 one-liners require quoting SQL and setting output modes manually; an SQLite MCP server exposes typed list_tables, describe_table, and read_query tools over the local database file.

label: AWS API MCP Server
replaces: Replaces repeated shell invocations of the `aws` CLI for inspecting and managing AWS resources with structured MCP tool calls.
rationale: AWS CLI commands require remembering service-specific flags, pagination tokens, and JMESPath filters; the official AWS Labs API MCP server validates CLI operations and returns structured AWS responses with explicit region scoping.

label: NPM Scripts MCP Server
replaces: Replaces repeated shell invocations of `npm`, `npx`, `yarn`, or `pnpm` scripts with structured MCP tool calls derived from package.json.
rationale: Ad-hoc package-manager shell calls risk mistyped script names and unguarded flags; an npm-scripts MCP server exposes only the project's declared package.json scripts as discoverable, whitelisted tools.

label: HTTP Fetch MCP Server
replaces: Replaces repeated shell HTTP requests via `curl`, `wget`, or HTTPie (`http`) with structured MCP fetch calls.
rationale: Raw curl and wget responses dump full HTML, headers, and progress noise into the conversation; the official MCP Fetch server converts web content into compact Markdown with bounded length and SSRF protections.
